blocks.text: Proxys.io in 2026: what you get

PROXYS.IO offers both rented static addresses and a rotating residential network. The provider reports more than 100 million ISP addresses across 195 countries, country/region/city targeting, up to 100 saved parameter sets and rotation every 2-60 minutes. Its mobile service covers 14 countries with city/carrier selection and roughly 2,000-5,000 addresses per country/carrier combination. Static IPv4 covers 24 markets. These are supplied specifications, not independently measured availability. HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5 are included on every plan.

Strengths: Low-entry per-address products; a provider-reported 100M+ residential network; country, region and city targeting; HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 included; a 24-hour refund window. Weak spots: Rotating mobile traffic pricing must be checked in the cart; residential plans have 30/60/90-day validity; published pool totals do not guarantee reachable IPs; independent target-specific performance has not been established here.
IPRoyal in 2026: what you get

IPRoyal is a value-focused provider best known for residential traffic that never expires. You can buy a single gigabyte, use it over months, and top up when you need to, which suits irregular projects better than monthly allowances. The residential pool is advertised at 32M+ IPs across 195 countries with state and city targeting, and sticky sessions can be requested for up to seven days. IPRoyal also sells ISP, datacenter and mobile proxies and a Web Unblocker billed per successful request.

Strengths: Residential traffic that does not expire; Sticky sessions up to 7 days; Can start with a single gigabyte; Several proxy types plus Web Unblocker in one account. Weak spots: Smaller pool than the enterprise networks; Headline $1.75/GB rate needs a 10 TB purchase; Mid-volume prices are not published.
Pricing: Proxys.io vs IPRoyal

PROXYS.IO separates traffic-based plans from per-address rentals. Rotating residential starts at $1.50/GB on 30, 60 or 90-day plans, without an IP or session cap. Static monthly starting prices are IPv6 $0.13, dynamic $0.27, shared IPv4 $0.67 (up to three users), foreign individual IPv4 $1.47, Windows-fingerprint IPv4 $1.87 and premium static residential IPv4 $3.60. Dedicated mobile IPv4 with unlimited traffic on a private channel starts at $56.79/month. Rotating mobile traffic is priced by the cart slider; no single starting per-GB rate has been confirmed. HEAT_RES provides 35% off eligible residential pay-per-traffic plans. Minimum static rental is one month and the refund window is 24 hours.

IPRoyal's residential subscription costs $7 for 1 GB, $11.90 for 2 GB and $52.50 for 10 GB ($5.25/GB); pay-as-you-go is 5% more ($7.35 for 1 GB). The advertised $1.75/GB rate applies only at 10 TB. Prices for custom volumes such as 25, 100 or 500 GB are calculated in the dashboard.

At 10 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; IPRoyal comes to about $52.50. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io and IPRoyal do not publish an exact price for that volume. Look past the per-GB figure too. IPRoyal lets unused traffic carry forward, while Proxys.io's allowance does not (rental periods (days or months)). For irregular workloads, that difference can outweigh a small gap in list price.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

PROXYS.IO reports a residential pool of 100M+ ISP addresses; this has not been independently audited. Proxys.io reports 100M+ addresses and IPRoyal lists '32M+'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, Proxys.io lists 195 residential countries, with separate mobile and static coverage countries and IPRoyal lists 195. On targeting, Proxys.io offers country, region and city for residential traffic, with city/carrier selection for mobile, while IPRoyal offers country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification).
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Proxys.io offers static per-IP proxies; rotating residential and mobile, and IPRoyal offers rotating or sticky sessions from 1 second up to 7 days. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?
General web scraping: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: solid success rates and non-expiring traffic for bursty crawls. How Proxys.io compares: it is a per-IP shop, not a large rotating pool.

SERP and rank tracking: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. Proxys.io: cheap IPv6 can handle some search tasks. IPRoyal: it works, but it has no dedicated SERP product. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Social media and multi-account management: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With Proxys.io: fixed dedicated or mobile IPs per account. With IPRoyal: 7-day sticky sessions keep one IP on one account. Run the same small test on both before committing.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: city targeting with pay-only-for-what-you-use traffic. How Proxys.io compares: limited rotation for large catalog crawls.
Ad verification and geo-testing: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: decent coverage but no ASN or carrier targeting on standard accounts. How Proxys.io compares: limited geo depth.

Tight budgets: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With Proxys.io: cheap per-IP rentals with unlimited bandwidth. With IPRoyal: small entry purchases and traffic that never expires. Run the same small test on both before committing.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial. IPRoyal: No general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies. Verification and payment rules differ too. Proxys.io: Light; crypto accepted. IPRoyal: Optional ID verification; required for ISP-level targeting and PayPal. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Proxys.io and IPRoyal before you commit
The quickest way to choose between Proxys.io and IPRoyal is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial; IPRoyal: no general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.

3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country. 4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Proxys.io comes out ahead in 0, IPRoyal in 3, and 3 are ties. That makes IPRoyal the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Proxys.io is strongest for multi-account and affiliate work that needs fixed IPs, while IPRoyal is strongest for irregular or seasonal projects. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
